Read the summary of the Terms of use. It\'s quick and important so you can use PushLife safely.

PushLife\'s workouts, stretches and tips follow published research and guidelines (such as the WHO\'s on physical activity), but the app has not been reviewed or certified by trainers, doctors or physiotherapists and does not replace professional guidance.
Your screen goal, daily free time, workout level and suggestions adjust to your preferences and your pace. You can change everything in Profile anytime.

Stop right away if you feel pain, dizziness or shortness of breath. If you have a health condition, an injury, are pregnant or haven\'t exercised in a long time, talk to a doctor first. You use the workouts at your own risk.
The camera counts exercises on the device itself. No photo or video is recorded or sent anywhere.
If you turn it on, the app uses usage access and a local VPN to block the apps you choose and adult sites. PushLife does not store or send what you browse.

Use the app responsibly and don\'t try to tamper with other people\'s accounts. Your account only stores your progress and you can delete it anytime. The terms may change; if they do, we\'ll ask you to accept again.

Exercise only changes your body when it follows a few principles. PushLife\'s programs are built on them:
Your body adapts to what you ask of it. If training never changes, progress stops. That\'s why the level rises bit by bit: more reps or a harder variation (wall → incline → knees → floor).
The WHO recommends muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week, plus 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity. Strength programs use 3 workouts a week.
Training is the stimulus; recovery happens afterwards. Leave about 48 h between workouts for the same muscle and sleep 7 to 9 hours a night.

In the first 2 to 4 weeks you get stronger because your brain learns to use the muscle better. Visible changes usually show up after 6 to 8 weeks of consistency. That\'s why programs last 4 to 6 weeks.
Holding each stretch for 15 to 30 seconds, at least 2 to 3 times a week (daily is better), improves flexibility within a few weeks. Stretch to tension, never to pain.

To build muscle, eat protein at every meal (eggs, chicken, meat, fish, beans, milk). People who strength train usually need 1.2 to 2 g of protein per kg of body weight per day. Prefer real food over ultra-processed food.
Drink water throughout the day and a little before and after training. A good sign: light-colored pee.

Every day you get half of your screen goal for free (1 h goal → 30 min). The rest you earn by training: the first program you do each day gives a bonus (based on how much you did), and a full week gives more.
Always warm up first. Stop if you feel sharp pain, dizziness or shortness of breath. If you have a health condition, an injury or are pregnant, talk to a doctor before starting.

Sources: WHO guidelines on physical activity (2020), American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) and International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) recommendations. The app is not certified by experts.
